item.title: Santa Rosa County opens free vegetative debris drop-off sites
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is opening two temporary, free drop-off locations for residents to dispose of vegetative debris from Hurricane Isaias, offering an alternative to the county's ongoing curbside collection service. The sites are located at Lenny James Tolbert Memorial Park (Holley Ball Park) in Navarre at 3124 Bob Tolbert Road, and Santa Rosa…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is opening two temporary, free drop-off locations for residents to dispose of vegetative debris from Hurricane Isaias, offering an alternative to the county's ongoing curbside collection service.

The sites are located at Lenny James Tolbert Memorial Park (Holley Ball Park) in Navarre at 3124 Bob Tolbert Road, and Santa Rosa Soccer Park in Pace at 3360 Joppa Drive. Both operate from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., seven days a week, until further notice. The service is available at no cost to Santa Rosa County residents with valid ID or proof of residency.

The drop-off sites accept only vegetative storm debris, including tree limbs, branches, leaves, and yard waste. Residents cannot dispose of household garbage, construction debris, appliances, or commercial waste at these locations. Material in plastic bags will not be accepted; only paper bags are permitted. This option supplements the county's curbside debris pickup, which began Wednesday, October 14, along publicly owned roads.

item.title: Northview football stays undefeated; local students earn national honors
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County schools are celebrating a string of academic and athletic wins as the fall season moves into high gear. Northview High's football team remained undefeated Friday night with a dominant 35-0 shutout over Port St. Joe, improving to 4-0 in their first season competing in Class 1A. The Chiefs have made a resounding statement in their…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County schools are celebrating a string of academic and athletic wins as the fall season moves into high gear.

Northview High's football team remained undefeated Friday night with a dominant 35-0 shutout over Port St. Joe, improving to 4-0 in their first season competing in Class 1A. The Chiefs have made a resounding statement in their new classification, showing no signs of slowing down momentum.

On the academic side, several local students earned national recognition this month. Tate High senior Abigail Lynch was named a Commended Student in the 2027 National Merit Scholarship Program, joining more than 1.2 million high school students competing nationally. A Tate graduate also became one of two National Merit Finalists welcomed to the University of West Florida this fall, bringing UWF's total National Merit scholarship recipients to 20 since 2017.

Tate High also inducted 36 new members into the National Honor Society this week, based on scholarship, service, leadership, and character. Meanwhile, Ransom Middle welcomed new inductees into the National Junior Honor Society, and teacher Lauralee Best at Tate received a $1,000 award through the College Football Playoff Foundation's Extra Yard for Teachers program, earning national recognition for her classroom work.

item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare is bringing back "Howl-o-Ween," a free community event designed to help adoptable pets find homes. The event runs Saturday, Oct. 24 from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the Animal Welfare and Adoption Center at 200 W. Fairfield Drive.

All adoption fees will be waived for dogs, cats, puppies, and kittens during the event. Escambia County residents will pay a $15 licensing fee per adoption. Prospective adopters can complete adoptions the same day and browse available pets beforehand at 24petconnect.com.

Beyond adoptions, the event will feature food trucks, vendors, and pet resources for the community. Animal Welfare Director John Robinson said the department is grateful for support from Anderson Subaru and Cumulus Media in organizing the second annual "Howl-o-Ween" event, particularly as the community navigates recent challenges.

item.title: Florida Protects 1,500 Acres of Ranch Land from Development
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson announced Friday the permanent protection of nearly 1,500 acres of working cattle ranches through the state's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, preventing future development while keeping the operations active. The two properties—Mossy Island Ranch in Manatee County and Florida Commission…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson announced Friday the permanent protection of nearly 1,500 acres of working cattle ranches through the state's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, preventing future development while keeping the operations active.

The two properties—Mossy Island Ranch in Manatee County and Florida Commission Company Ranch in Highlands County—have been secured through rural lands protection easements totaling $8.7 million. Manatee County contributed $500,000 toward the Mossy Island protection. Both ranches are located within the Florida Wildlife Corridor and enrolled in the state's Best Management Practices program.

Mossy Island, a 420-acre cattle operation, sits adjacent to Myakka River State Park and faces development pressure as surrounding lands are projected to develop by 2040. The larger Florida Commission Company Ranch spans 1,046 acres and operates cattle grazing and hay production. By purchasing development rights rather than acquiring land outright, the program avoids long-term state ownership costs while supporting agricultural operations.

Since its 1999 establishment, the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program has permanently preserved more than 253,000 acres statewide. Under Simpson's administration alone, the program has protected nearly 188,000 acres, recognizing that Florida's working agricultural lands face increasing pressure from development and urban expansion.

item.title: AAA: Over a Third of Florida Drivers Ignore Move Over Law Despite Claims
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new AAA survey released ahead of National Slow Down, Move Over Day on October 17 reveals a troubling gap between what drivers say they do and what they actually do when approaching roadside emergencies. While more than 90% of drivers surveyed reported slowing down or moving over the last time they passed a disabled vehicle, tow truck, or police…
item.content:encoded:
A new AAA survey released ahead of National Slow Down, Move Over Day on October 17 reveals a troubling gap between what drivers say they do and what they actually do when approaching roadside emergencies. While more than 90% of drivers surveyed reported slowing down or moving over the last time they passed a disabled vehicle, tow truck, or police car on the shoulder, actual observational research tells a different story: only 64% of drivers actually changed lanes or reduced speed. That means more than one-third of drivers did neither.

The stakes are high. Between 2019 and 2023, more than 2,100 people were struck and killed while stranded or working at the roadside. In 2025 alone, AAA responded to more than 30 million roadside events, with 15 roadside service providers losing their lives in Slow Down, Move Over-related incidents — some involving impaired or hit-and-run drivers.

"Drivers often think roadside danger only affects police officers, firefighters, and tow truck operators," said Mark Jenkins, spokesman for AAA – The Auto Club Group. "But anyone can become vulnerable at the roadside. A flat tire, dead battery, or mechanical problem can place drivers and passengers just feet from moving traffic." AAA's survey also found that 56% of Floridians identified being struck by another vehicle as their biggest concern if their own vehicle became disabled.

In Florida, drivers are required by law to move over for all stopped vehicles displaying flashing or hazard lights, including law enforcement, EMS, fire, construction, and disabled vehicles. If changing lanes isn't safe, motorists must reduce speed and proceed with caution. AAA urges all drivers to heed the reminder: when you see flashing lights or a stopped vehicle ahead, slow down, move over when safe, and stay alert.

item.content:encoded:
If you've been thinking about serving your community, today is your deadline. Friday, October 16 is the final day to submit an application for two open seats on the West Florida Public Libraries Board of Governance, which oversees library service across all of Escambia County.

The board typically meets on the fourth Monday of each month at 4 p.m. Board members help guide policy and operations for the library system that serves the entire county. If you're interested in applying, you'll need to get your application in before the close of business today.

For details on how to apply and what's required, contact West Florida Public Libraries directly.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's Blue Wahoos Stadium will host the Savannah Bananas' Banana Ball World Tour in May 2027, the team announced Thursday. The two-day event brings the Bananas' high-energy, entertainment-focused baseball brand to Pensacola's bayfront venue.

Banana Ball, created by the Savannah Bananas, is known for its fast-paced gameplay, casual atmosphere, and fan-first approach to baseball. The exhibition tour has drawn crowds across the country with its unconventional rules and showmanship-heavy format.

The selection marks another major event for Blue Wahoos Stadium, which continues to host regional and national sporting events beyond the team's regular Minor League Baseball season. More details about dates, ticket information, and game times are expected to be announced.

item.content:encoded:

Hit-and-run crashes on local highways remain a serious concern for law enforcement. Drivers who witnessed the collision or have information about the fleeing vehicle are urged to contact the Florida Highway Patrol.

Friday will start with partly sunny skies and a high around 85 degrees, with winds remaining calm before picking up to around 5 mph from the west in the afternoon. Conditions…
item.content:encoded:
A cooling trend is heading to the North Escambia area, with winds expected to gust near 30 mph Friday night into Saturday, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Friday will start with partly sunny skies and a high around 85 degrees, with winds remaining calm before picking up to around 5 mph from the west in the afternoon. Conditions will shift as evening approaches, with mostly cloudy skies gradually clearing out overnight.

Lows are expected to dip to around 54 degrees Friday night as the cooler air mass moves in. Residents should prepare for the gusty winds, which could affect outdoor activities and loose debris throughout the evening and into Saturday.

item.title: Escambia County moves forward with master plan for former OLF-8 in Beulah
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners took a significant step Thursday toward establishing zoning and regulatory guidelines for the former Outlying Landing Field 8 property in Beulah, advancing an ordinance that would adopt an updated master plan and design code for the site. The action brings the county closer to finalizing how the…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Board of County Commissioners took a significant step Thursday toward establishing zoning and regulatory guidelines for the former Outlying Landing Field 8 property in Beulah, advancing an ordinance that would adopt an updated master plan and design code for the site.

The action brings the county closer to finalizing how the property — a former Naval auxiliary airfield — will be developed and used going forward. The updated master plan and design code would set standards for future construction and land use on the OLF-8 site, addressing everything from building guidelines to infrastructure requirements.

Thursday's vote by the commissioners moved the ordinance forward in the approval process. The property has sat largely undeveloped since its Naval use ended, and county officials have been working to create a coherent development vision that balances economic opportunity with community interests in the Beulah area.

item.title: Free Pet Food Giveaway Today at PJ's Coffee; Salzman Hosts Storm Recovery Event
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State Representative Michelle Salzman is hosting a free pet food distribution today from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at PJ's Coffee, 85 W Airport Blvd in Pensacola, aimed at helping local families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event, sponsored by the Walmart Foundation and organized in partnership with Jennifer Harrison, will provide both dog…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman is hosting a free pet food distribution today from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. at PJ's Coffee, 85 W Airport Blvd in Pensacola, aimed at helping local families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias.

The event, sponsored by the Walmart Foundation and organized in partnership with Jennifer Harrison, will provide both dog and cat food to pet owners facing added expenses during storm recovery. Salzman said the distribution recognizes that pets are an important part of households and that ensuring they're fed is part of easing the broader burden families face after a hurricane. "By working together, we can help ensure that families and their pets have the support they need as we continue moving forward," she said in a statement.

PJ's Coffee is providing the venue at no cost and will offer free hot or iced coffee to everyone who attends. Salzman also noted that residents can contact their local animal shelter, which is offering additional pet assistance programs for those seeking help during the recovery period.

The scope and cause of the outage were not immediately detailed in the available reporting. Residents and business owners in the affected area are urged to monitor updates from local utilities and city officials for restoration timelines.

item.title: DeSantis Unveils Christopher Columbus Statue in Naples
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled a statue of Christopher Columbus in Naples on Wednesday as part of Florida's America250 initiative marking the nation's 250th anniversary. The Italian explorer's likeness was installed in a city that shares its name with the Italian metropolitan area, creating what state officials say is a fitting connection to…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled a statue of Christopher Columbus in Naples on Wednesday as part of Florida's America250 initiative marking the nation's 250th anniversary. The Italian explorer's likeness was installed in a city that shares its name with the Italian metropolitan area, creating what state officials say is a fitting connection to Columbus's heritage.

The statue commemorates Columbus's voyages beginning in 1492, which opened transatlantic exploration and eventually led to European settlement of the Americas, including Florida. State officials noted that Columbus's expeditions inspired subsequent explorers who shaped early Florida, including Juan Ponce de León and Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, who founded St. Augustine in 1565.

"Columbus remains an important figure in Italian-American heritage and a prominent part of the history of Western exploration," the Governor's office said in a statement. Michele Mistò, Consul General of Italy in Miami, called the unveiling an important recognition during Italian-American Heritage Month, noting Italy's ongoing contributions to Florida's economy and culture.

The Naples monument is part of DeSantis's broader effort to preserve American history through the America250 initiative. In February 2025, the Governor announced plans to install additional statues honoring the Founding Fathers, including George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Franklin, James Madison, James Monroe, and Alexander Hamilton.

item.title: Jack Brewer Foundation distributes 1,000 free meals in Milton today

item.description: The Jack Brewer Foundation is back at Jernigan's Landing in Milton today with free prepared meals for residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The distribution runs at noon and 6 p.m., with 1,000 meals available on a first-come, first-served basis — up to four per vehicle. The City of Milton has set up a traffic route to keep things…
item.content:encoded:
The Jack Brewer Foundation is back at Jernigan's Landing in Milton today with free prepared meals for residents still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The distribution runs at noon and 6 p.m., with 1,000 meals available on a first-come, first-served basis — up to four per vehicle.

The City of Milton has set up a traffic route to keep things moving: drivers enter from Canal Street, turn left onto Pine Street, then left onto South Willing Street for pickup. After grabbing meals, head right onto Elmira Street and exit via Oak Street.

If you or someone you know needs a meal, head out to Jernigan's Landing today. The foundation has been a steady presence in the community's hurricane recovery effort.
